content:
As mentioned earlier, the Google Chrome browser has now switched to a bi-weekly release cycle.

Previously, Chrome had a major "milestone" update every four weeks, such as jumping from version 100 to version 101; before 2021, Google used a six-week cycle.

The move to a major update every two weeks is intended to "roll out new features, performance improvements, and bug fixes more quickly." Each update will contain fewer changes, but be released more frequently.

Google also pointed out that this "accelerated pace benefits the entire web ecosystem." Developers will be able to "roll out modern web features more reliably, because interoperability updates can be delivered more quickly within a shorter deployment window, and security improvements can also reach users across platforms faster." Each "smaller-scope release" also helps "identify regressions more quickly."

On the security front, Google said that in the face of threats brought about by the rise of artificial intelligence, this change helps "respond to rapidly evolving threats."

For enterprise customers, Chrome offers an "Extended Stable" channel, which updates every eight weeks: version 156 will be released first, followed by version 160. Google said that most enterprise users should adopt the Stable channel, which updates every two weeks.

Chrome version 153 is launching today on desktop, Android, and iOS platforms, with version 154 scheduled for release on September 22.
